slot.brief: Two-draw or card-die scenario; ask P(A|B) or check independence of two events from a joint table

stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard $52$-card deck. Given that at least one is a queen, the probability that both are face cards (J, Q or K) is

verdicts.working: Favorable pairs: \(\binom{12}{2}-\binom{8}{2}=38\) (both face cards, with at least one queen). Pairs with at least one queen: \(\binom{52}{2}-\binom{48}{2}=198\). Thus the probability is \(38/198=19/99\).

working:
Pairs with at least one queen: $\binom{52}{2}-\binom{48}{2}=198$. Favorable pairs: $\binom{12}{2}-\binom{8}{2}=38$. Hence $P=\dfrac{38}{198}=\dfrac{19}{99}$.

Independent check: Favorable pairs: \(\binom{12}{2}-\binom{8}{2}=38\) (both face cards, with at least one queen). Pairs with at least one queen: \(\binom{52}{2}-\binom{48}{2}=198\). Thus the probability is \(38/198=19/99\).
solution:
Pairs with at least one queen: $\binom{52}{2}-\binom{48}{2}=198$. Favorable pairs (both face cards and at least one queen): $\binom{12}{2}-\binom{8}{2}=38$.
$$P=\frac{38}{198}=\frac{19}{99}$$
